# Zhex

> Zhex is a Forth-inspired programming language built on small words and big ideas: compact code with visible flow, meaningful names, and checked types, executed by a working Go interpreter. Every program is checked — names, types, and word connections — before any of it runs.

## Docs

- [Manifesto](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/manifesto.html): the intentions behind Zhex — visible data, small composed words, a language machines can read, errors that teach, performance you can measure, and code humans enjoy reviewing. Full text at docs/manifesto.md; concrete goals at docs/language-goals.md.
- [Docs](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs.html): a grouped guide to getting started, language concepts, the standard library, and tools, with separate topic pages.
- [Getting started](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/getting-started.html): install and run a first program.
- [Language](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/syntax.html): syntax, values, words, flows, control flow, Results, and modules.
- Block values: `if`, `match`, and `flow` can be the entire right-hand side of a `let`, `var`, or assignment; the block's final value is used. They are not general nested expressions or call arguments.
- Multiline syntax: expressions may continue inside `()`, `[]`, and `{}`; blank and comment-only lines are allowed while a delimiter is open. Trailing commas are rejected, and `<...>` type arguments do not open a continuation.
- Simple word calls: parenthesized calls remain valid; a simple call may omit call parentheses at a complete statement, binding/assignment right-hand side, final word value, or flow step. Commas separate arguments (`add 1, 2`); whitespace alone does not. `print 1 + 1` passes one arithmetic result. Keep nested calls parenthesized (`print(add(1, 2))`) and use parentheses for negative or list-literal first arguments; `values [0]` remains indexing. A bare word name in expression position calls an accessible zero-argument word, while a same-named value binding is a value. A flow step receives the current value as its first argument, then any comma-separated extra arguments.
- [Calls and defaults](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/calls.html): simple comma-separated word-call syntax, zero-argument calls, flow arguments, and boundaries where parentheses remain necessary.
- [Records and named types](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/records.html): nominal record declarations, positional or named construction, field defaults, immutable fields, and explicit type annotations.
- [Choices and matching](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/choices.html): concrete named alternatives, payload binding, exhaustive cases, and a final `case _` default.
- [Lists and arrays](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/collections.html): homogeneous shared collections, checked indexing, resizing, limits, and failure handling.
- [Maps](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/maps.html): typed inferred keys and values, `Option` lookup, insertion-ordered iteration, updates, and flows.
- [Dates and time zones](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/temporal.html): calendar dates, elapsed durations, instants, named IANA zones, and DST-aware operations.
- [JSON](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/json.html): typed JSON decoding with record defaults, strict validation and field paths, and encoding of supported values.
- [Collection iteration](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/iteration.html): list indices, array coordinates, row-major arrays, insertion-ordered map traversal, and mutation guards.
- Rich-value rules: record declarations and choices are nominal. Record constructors accept all-positional arguments in field order or all-named arguments in any field order; the forms cannot mix. Trailing defaults may be omitted, and evaluate after supplied arguments in declaration order. Named arguments apply only to record constructors, not words, built-ins, or choice alternatives. `type Names = alias List<String>` defines a transparent alias. Fields are immutable; choice alternatives are constructed by qualified name, with payloads in declared order. A choice may have one type parameter: payload constructors infer it, while a nullary alternative needs an expected type. Generic records and words are not supported. Match every alternative once, or use one final `case _`; a default after all named alternatives is an error. Choices cannot be printed or compared directly, payloads cannot contain `Result`, and caught concrete errors need `error.wrap` before storing in an `Error` payload. Lists infer homogeneous elements; empty list values need an expected `List<T>`. Arrays use explicit `List<Int>` shapes, rank 2..32, and at most 1,000,000 elements. List/array reads, `array.new`, `list.append`, and `array.resize` return ordinary values and diagnose invalid operations at runtime; direct `try` or `catch` selects a checked Result for that operation only. Plain indexed writes return `Unit` and raise runtime diagnostics for invalid rank, bounds, or active-iteration mutation; parenthesized indexed writes return a checked `Result<Unit, Error>`. `Map<K, V>` infers types from nonempty literals; empty maps need an expected type. Map literal keys are constant `String`, `Int`, or `Bool` literals; dynamic keys are allowed for lookup, update, containment, and removal. Lookup yields `Option<V>` without `try`, and map values cannot contain `Result`. Map iteration preserves insertion order. Mutation of an actively traversed map raises a runtime `collection-iterating` diagnostic before changing storage; it is not a `Result`. Collection aliases share storage. Caught concrete errors may go directly to built-in `error.*` operations, but require `error.wrap` before passing to a user word expecting `Error` or storing in an Error-typed record field or collection; flow cannot pass Error values to user-defined steps.
- [Standard library](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/text.html): text, buffers, files, and console operations.
- JSON: `json.decode(raw, defaults)` infers the target from a typed default and returns `Result<T, Error>`; missing record fields use defaults, invalid supplied fields do not. Present Lists/Maps replace defaults, and each decoded value gets fresh copies of mutable defaults while aliases inside that value remain shared. `json.encode(value)` returns compact JSON; record fields follow declaration order and Map keys follow insertion order. Supported types are `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, records, `List<T>`, `Map<String, T>`, and `Option<T>` in nested combinations, except direct nested `Option<Option<T>>`; `null` means `Option.None`. Int accepts signed 64-bit integer-form JSON tokens only; decimal/exponent notation and overflow reject. Arrays, resources, Results, non-Option choices, and non-string-key maps are unsupported. JSON errors include `json-syntax`, `json-type`, `json-field`, `json-range`, and `json-depth`; `error.detail(error, "path")` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, with root as empty string and `~`/`/` escaped as `~0`/`~1`.
- [Tools](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/repl.html): the REPL, diagnostics, and editor support.
- Vocabulary: text work uses the `text.*` words — `length` (code points), `line-count`, `word-count`, `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `contains`, `index-of` (code-point position, `-1` when absent), `slice(start, end)` (code points, bounds clamp, `start >= end` is empty), `replace(old, new)` (every occurrence, literal, empty `old` errors), plus the earlier `reverse` and `to-int`. Lines build in a `Buffer`: `buffer.new()`, `buffer.add-line`, `buffer.line-count`, `buffer.line(i)` and `buffer.set-line(i, text)` (Results failing `buffer-range` on a bad index), `buffer.to-text`; `let` binds the buffer's name — two names observe one buffer — and `Buffer` is excluded from `==` and rejected by `print` (convert with `buffer.to-text`). Files read whole (`file.read-all(path)` to String, `file.read-lines(path)` to a Buffer of chomped lines) or streamed (`file.open(path)`, `file.read-line(f)` where end of file fails inside the Result, `file.close(f)` idempotent); `for line in file.lines(path)` streams chomped lines and guarantees the close on every exit, including loop-body failures. File Results fail `file-open`, `file-read`, or `file-utf8`, naming the path and the operating system's reason. Program arguments forward as `zhex run file.zhex [args...]`: read them with `console.args-count()` and `console.arg(i)` (a Result failing `argument-missing` on a bad index).
- Results and errors: built-ins return explicit `Result<T, E>`. Word parameter annotations may be omitted when body and same-program call constraints determine one concrete type; unresolved parameters need annotations, conflicting calls are type errors, and `Result` cannot be a word parameter. Trailing word parameters may have defaults; required parameters come first and calls remain positional. Defaults can infer parameter types, run lazily only when omitted, and evaluate after supplied arguments (source order) in parameter order. They use declaring-module scope, cannot reference parameters/globals/caller bindings or let a `Result` escape, and are fresh on each call; `words` displays `= ...`. Compatible REPL redefinitions affect new entries while checked callers retain the earlier word/defaults. Return annotations may also be omitted when the body determines one concrete success type. An escaping `try` infers one error family and the effective Result signature, and successful values are wrapped once. Pure words keep their inferred or annotated type. A recursive cycle without a concrete type anchor, empty collection, or nullary `Option.None` needs a return annotation. Explicit `Result<T, E>` signatures remain supported with `ok`/`err`, without wrapping twice. Each caller still uses `try` or `catch`; multiple uncaught families in one word are rejected, so catch a failure or explicitly wrap it as common `Error`. Runtime faults are not inferred. `catch [name]` lazily supplies a same-typed fallback or exits via `console.exit`/`console.fail`. Bare Results cannot be discarded; a stored `let pending = call()` must be handled by the immediately following same-block statement as exactly `pending try` or `pending catch ...`, standalone or as a whole new `let` RHS. Explicit flow steps use `word-name try`. `error.new` creates a cause-less application Error; `error.wrap` converts to common `Error` and preserves the cause; accessors include code/message/operation/file/line/column/detail/has-cause/cause. File detail `reason` values are `not-found`, `permission-denied`, `other` (open), and `invalid-utf8`, `closed`, `read-failed`, `end-of-file` (read). `error.set-reporter(named-word)` installs a top-level `(Error) -> Unit` callback. `error.report(problem)` reports a handled occurrence; a failure escaping the program calls the reporter once before the diagnostic. Intermediate propagation does not report, duplicate occurrences are suppressed, callback failure/recursion is isolated, and no external destination is configured by default. `console.exit(status)` ends execution with 0..255, and `console.fail(message)` writes to stderr and ends with status 1; neither reports a valid deliberate exit. Out-of-range exit status is a runtime diagnostic. These exits close active `file.lines` streams; explicitly opened files still require `file.close`. Reporter calls to either operation cannot replace the original outcome.
- Modules: split a program across files with `use math` — it loads the sibling `math.zhex` next to the importing file (each file's own imports resolve beside it; the REPL resolves against the working directory and adopts the module for the session). Imported words are called qualified (`math.gcd(a, b)`); module words call each other bare inside their own file and cannot see the importer's words; a module's own imports stay private to it, and two modules never collide. A leading underscore makes a word or type module-private: calling one from outside fails `private-use`, and it is never suggested cross-module. A public signature, record field, or choice payload cannot expose a private type, even through a List, Array, Map, or Result. Imported choice constructors and cases are qualified (`model.Status.Ready`). Errors: a missing module fails `use-missing` naming the searched path; import cycles fail `use-cycle` spelling the files; module names `text`, `int`, `buffer`, `file`, `console`, `error`, `list`, `array`, `map`, and `json` fail `use-reserved`; the built-in `Option` type and constructors are reserved names, but `Option` is not a reserved module name. Imported files may declare words and types but top-level statements fail `module-body`; `use` outside a file's top level fails `use-location` — and `use` is a reserved word. Loaded modules check before their importers, and module errors annotate the module's own source. Trace events carry qualified names (`{"word":"math.gcd"}`, module-private words included) with word returns pointing into the module file (`{"file":"math.zhex"}`). Corpus example: `examples/modules/main.zhex`, a two-file program run as `zhex run examples/modules/main.zhex`.
- [Examples](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples.html): runnable programs with source, sample input, and real output — the source and output on the page are produced by the actual interpreter. `text-stats` is the first real application: run it as `zhex run examples/text-stats.zhex <file> [upper]` — one argument reports the file's line, word, and character counts from one whole read, and any second argument streams the file uppercased line by line.
- [Roadmap](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/roadmap.html): what is done, what is next, and what is future, mirrored by a public project board.
- [Error catalog](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html): built-in diagnostic codes with their meanings and fixes; application codes from `error.new`/`error.wrap` are not catalog entries. Diagnostics print `file:line:column: message` plus an excerpt, caret, and `hint:` line; `zhex run file.zhex --report=json` emits the machine-readable report `{code, severity, file, line, column, message, hint}`, plus optional additive span_start_column/span_end_column (checker diagnostics with a span, never runtime).
- [Development insight](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/diagnostics-plan.md): `zhex run file.zhex --trace` streams JSONL step events to stderr — one JSON object per line, emitted before any diagnostic, and combinable with `--report=json` (events, then the report). Four events: `{"event":"word-call","word":W,"file":F,"line":N,"args":[...]}`, `{"event":"binding","name":N,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"flow-step","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"word-return","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`. `word-call` fires only for program words — builtins never emit it; they appear as flow-step or binding effects. Bindings holding a `Result` (a read without postfix `try`) render `ok("inner")` or `err("message")`; other values render per the checker's static types — Int as digits, Bool as `true`/`false`, String verbatim, Unit as the empty string, Buffer as `buffer(<n> lines)`, File as `file("<path>")` — and a `-> Unit` word returns value "". Tracing never fails a run, and output without the flag is unchanged.
- REPL: `zhex repl [--trace]` runs an interactive session where words and values persist across entries; calls use parentheses (`print(1 + 1)`) or the simple comma-separated form (`print 1 + 1`). In a terminal, pending blocks prefill editable indentation; Tab inserts four spaces, Backspace removes one character; four presses dedent one level. An empty or spaces-only continuation line submits, except blank and comment-only lines inside open `()`, `[]`, or `{}`. Closing a completed top-level expression submits it immediately; a pending block still needs a blank line. While editing, Ctrl-C cancels the current entry; Ctrl-D on an empty top-level line exits 0; in a pending entry, an empty or spaces-only continuation line discards the entry and exits. Bracketed paste preserves source indentation. Piped entries retain line-based behavior and need explicit four-space block indentation; tabs and non-ASCII whitespace outside strings or comments remain source errors. An unclosed delimiter at piped EOF is a syntax error. Program `read-line` uses the same terminal reader without source auto-indentation or Tab expansion. Agents can script a session by piping entries to standard input. A blank line ends a multi-line entry when no delimiter is open; a missing indented block or open delimiter continues it. Bare ordinary expressions echo their value; naked Result expressions are rejected and must be handled with `try` or `catch` in the same entry. `words` lists effective parameter, return, and Result signatures sorted by name and shadows a user binding of that name; a word can be redefined with the same effective signature, while an incompatible signature change is rejected transactionally. Parameter inference must resolve within the defining entry. `let` shadows silently. Check and runtime errors print the annotated diagnostic and the session survives; a runtime error keeps the entry's earlier effects. A final input line without a trailing newline still runs. Ctrl-D or the preloaded ordinary REPL word `bye()` exits 0; the zero-argument call form `bye` is equivalent. `bye()` appears in `words`, follows normal redefinition rules, and is unavailable in source files. With `--trace`, the same JSONL step events as `zhex run` stream to stderr with `"file":"repl"`.

## Reference

- [Language contract](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/initial-language.md): the authoritative syntax and semantics the interpreter enforces.
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for writing correct Zhex and verifying changes with the executable test suite.
- [Example sources](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples/hello.zhex): downloadable `.zhex` files — swap the filename for fizzbuzz, fibonacci, gcd, times-table, factorial, palindrome, composition, calls, records, choices, collections, maps, json-config, word-defaults, temporal, life, edit-distance, text-stats, recovery, or exit-status; the two-file modules program lives at examples/modules/main.zhex with its math.zhex beside it.
- [Project board](https://github.com/users/desireco/projects/8): the backlog and delivered work as issues on a public Kanban board.
